He won the North American Amateur Snooker Championship in 1971 and was recommended to the WPBSA by world champion John Spencer, turning professional in 1972.

name: Björn Borg
milestone_by_age_26: Won the French Open at age 18 in 1974, becoming the youngest-ever Roland-Garros champion at the time; had already won the Wimbledon junior singles title at 15 in 1972 and represented Sweden in Davis Cup at 15.
early_history_summary: Borg was born in Stockholm, Sweden, the only child of Rune, an electrician, and Margaretha Borg. He began playing tennis at age 9 after his father won a golden tennis racket at a table-tennis tournament. By 15, he was representing Sweden in the Davis Cup and won the Wimbledon junior title. He turned professional at 16 and won his first Grand Slam at the 1974 French Open at age 18.

evidence_summary: Borg was a textbook child prodigy who began tennis at 9, reached the Swedish Davis Cup team at 15, won junior Wimbledon at 15-16, and claimed his first Grand Slam at the French Open at 18. His father, an electrician, gave him a tennis racket won at a table-tennis tournament, which launched his career. Borg's revolutionary topspin and two-handed backhand made him a dominant force from his teenage years. He came from a working-class family in Södertälje with no prior tennis connections.
